definitions.explanation: A state of being completely worn out in body and mind. A formal, written-style word that almost always appears in the set phrase {疲労困憊|ひろうこんぱい} ('worn out with fatigue').

examples.japanese: {疲労|ひろう}{困憊|こんぱい}で{動|うご}けない。
{連日|れんじつ}の{残業|ざんぎょう}で{困憊|こんぱい}している。
examples.english: I'm worn out from working overtime day after day.

examples.japanese: {長時間|ちょうじかん}の{看病|かんびょう}で、{家族|かぞく}は{心身|しんしん}ともに{困憊|こんぱい}していた。
examples.english: From the long hours of nursing care, the family was exhausted in both body and mind.

notes:
A formal, written-style noun meaning utter exhaustion. In practice it rarely stands alone — it nearly always appears in the four-character phrase {疲労困憊|ひろうこんぱい}. Also used with する ({困憊|こんぱい}する).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {疲労|ひろう}{困憊|こんぱい}: worn out with fatigue
- {心身|しんしん}ともに{困憊|こんぱい}する: to be exhausted in body and mind
- {困憊|こんぱい}しきる: to be completely worn out

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {疲労|ひろう}: fatigue; tiredness — everyday word; {困憊|こんぱい} is stronger and more literary
- へとへと: worn out; dead tired — colloquial and vivid, used in casual speech
